servers.name: Pax8
servers.description: Pax8 marketplace: companies, product catalogue, subscriptions, orders and invoices, via Pax8's own hosted MCP server.

credentials.label: Pax8 MCP token
credentials.help: Pax8 Partner Portal > Integrations > MCP (app.pax8.com/integrations/mcp)

writes: Provision, modify and cancel client subscriptions

warnings.risk: Can order and cancel client subscriptions
warnings.detail: The plugin lists provisioning, modifying and cancelling cloud subscriptions and placing orders. A change here alters a client's services and your billing. Keep it read-only unless you need to order through Claude.

warnings.risk: Hosted by Pax8
warnings.detail: The MCP server is Pax8's own, hosted at mcp.pax8.com. Your token and the data Claude reads go to Pax8, the vendor you already use. The skills come from WYRE's plugin.

servers.name: HaloPSA
servers.description: Tickets, clients, sites, contacts, assets and contracts in HaloPSA.

credentials.label: HaloPSA tenant
credentials.help: The part before .halopsa.com in your HaloPSA address, e.g. yourmsp

credentials.label: OAuth client ID
credentials.help: Configuration > Integrations > HaloPSA API > View Applications

credentials.label: OAuth client secret
credentials.help: Same screen. Use Client Credentials.
credentials.leastPrivilege: Create a dedicated API application with only the permissions you need. Leave write permissions off unless you turn on writes.

writes: Create and update tickets, actions and attachments
Create, update and delete clients, sites and contacts

warnings.risk: Credentials and data pass through a third party
warnings.detail: By default the plugin connects to an MCP server hosted by WYRE at halopsa-mcp.wyre.workers.dev, not by HaloPSA. Your HaloPSA client secret and the ticket data Claude reads pass through it. How credentials reach that server isn't documented yet, so Tabby9 doesn't offer an install.

warnings.risk: Setup guide stores the secret in plain text
warnings.detail: The plugin's recommended setup puts HALOPSA_CLIENT_SECRET in ~/.claude/settings.json, a plain-text file that backups and sync tools copy. Don't follow that step.

warnings.risk: Reads text written by outsiders
warnings.detail: Ticket text comes from end users and email. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

servers.name: ConnectWise PSA (mspstack)
servers.description: Tickets, time, schedule, companies, configurations and invoices in ConnectWise PSA, grouped into toolsets per role. Runs on your PC.

credentials.label: ConnectWise host
credentials.help: Your ConnectWise API host, e.g. api-au.myconnectwise.net, or your on-prem host

credentials.label: Company ID
credentials.help: The company identifier you sign in with

credentials.label: Client ID
credentials.help: Register an integration at developer.connectwise.com

credentials.label: Public key
credentials.help: System > Members > API Members > API Keys

credentials.label: Private key
credentials.leastPrivilege: A dedicated API member whose security role covers only the boards and modules you need. ConnectWise applies that role to every tool.

credentials.label: Member identifier
credentials.help: The member the keys belong to; used by the my-tickets and my-time tools

reads: Tickets, notes, tasks and ticket time
writes: Create and update tickets, add notes, merge (bundle) tickets
Create and update time entries, submit timesheets
Schedule tickets, update and delete schedule entries

warnings.risk: Reads text written by outsiders
warnings.detail: Ticket text comes from end users and email. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

warnings.risk: Dependencies are resolved when you install
warnings.detail: The npm package doesn't ship a lockfile, so installing it fetches whatever dependency versions match its ranges that day. The repository's own lockfile pins versions with published advisories, including the MCP SDK.

warnings.risk: Optional database access stays off
warnings.detail: An optional on-prem SQL toolset reads the whole Manage database through one shared read-only login, bypassing each member's permissions. It turns on only when CW_DB_* settings exist; Tabby9 doesn't set them.

servers.name: ConnectWise Automate

credentials.label: Automate server
credentials.help: Your Automate server hostname

credentials.label: Integrator password
credentials.leastPrivilege: An integrator account limited to what you need; don't use a full admin login

writes: Change monitoring templates, thresholds and assignments
Acknowledge alerts and create tickets from them

warnings.risk: Can run scripts on client computers
warnings.detail: The plugin lists running scripts on computers across all clients. One wrong call runs code on client machines. Keep it read-only unless you have a specific need, and keep Claude Code's approval prompt in front of every script run.

warnings.risk: Credentials and data pass through a third party
warnings.detail: By default the plugin connects to an MCP server hosted by WYRE at connectwise-automate-mcp.wyre.workers.dev, not by ConnectWise. Your integrator password passes through it. How credentials reach that server isn't documented yet, so Tabby9 doesn't offer an install.

servers.name: NinjaOne
servers.description: Devices, organisations, locations, alerts and tickets in NinjaOne.

credentials.label: Region
credentials.help: us, eu or oc

credentials.label: OAuth client ID
credentials.help: Administration > Apps > API > Client App IDs

credentials.label: OAuth client secret
credentials.leastPrivilege: A client-credentials app with the monitoring scope only. Add management only if you turn on writes.

warnings.risk: Credentials and data pass through a third party

servers.name: Datto RMM
servers.description: Sites, devices, alerts, jobs and audits in Datto RMM, with a local copy of your fleet for fleet-wide questions.

credentials.label: Platform
credentials.help: Your Datto RMM region: pinotage, merlot, concord, vidal, zinfandel or syrah

credentials.label: API key
credentials.help: Setup > Users > generate API keys

credentials.label: API secret key
credentials.leastPrivilege: A dedicated API user. API access is all-or-nothing per user in Datto RMM, so give that user a read-only security level.

writes: Every Datto RMM API operation the user's role allows, including jobs on devices

warnings.risk: Can start jobs on client devices
warnings.detail: It covers every Datto RMM API operation, which includes starting jobs (components) on devices. One wrong call runs code on client machines. Use an API user with a read-only security level unless you need changes.

warnings.risk: Keeps a local copy of your fleet
warnings.detail: It syncs your Datto RMM sites, devices, alerts and audits into a SQLite file under your Windows user profile. Anyone or any program with access to your account can read it.

warnings.risk: HTTP mode in this version is unsafe
warnings.detail: Its maintainer warns that this version's HTTP mode has no password, listens on every network interface and can be reached by a web page you open. Tabby9 runs it only in its default local (stdio) mode.

servers.name: CIPP + Microsoft 365
servers.description: Entra ID, Intune, Exchange Online, Defender and GDAP across every client tenant via your CIPP instance.

credentials.label: CIPP API URL
credentials.help: The URL CIPP shows for your API client. It must include /api.

credentials.label: Bearer token
credentials.help: A token for a CIPP API client (Integrations > CIPP-API)
credentials.leastPrivilege: Give the API client a read-only Custom Role, as the skill's own docs advise

writes: Changes CIPP can make in client tenants (shown as a preview; carried out only with --execute)

warnings.risk: Can change every client tenant
warnings.detail: CIPP reaches every client's Microsoft 365 tenant. With writes on, a change Claude makes can alter users, mailboxes or Conditional Access across clients. Keep the read-only switch on and give the CIPP API client a read-only role.

warnings.risk: Keeps a local copy of tenant data
warnings.detail: It keeps a local store of what it reads from your tenants, for history and offline questions, under your Windows user profile. Anyone or any program with access to your account can read it.
